haiku-low.q1: It returns the fallback, the popular-items list, marked as a fallback, and does not call the model.
haiku-low.q2: It keeps using the features the online store already has until a record is older than 6 hours. After that the record counts as missing and the fallback is returned.
haiku-low.q3: No. Shadow output is never shown to a user. A shadow failure is logged as an error and never slows or breaks the user's response.
haiku-low.q4: Users whose stable hash of user ID, modulo 100, is under 10. That is about 10%, and a user is always in or always out.
haiku-low.q5: At least 7 days in shadow, error rate under 0.5%, p99 inference latency under 80 ms, and the ML lead's approval.
haiku-low.q6: Undecided. Product has not decided whether a live A/B test goes between shadow and the full switch, so the plan does not choose.
haiku-low.q7: Each instance checks the registry every 15 seconds. When active points to a new version, it loads it in the background, runs the feature check, and swaps only on success. No redeploy.
haiku-low.q8: After responding, the API queues the user ID and its already-fetched features without waiting. Separate shadow workers read the queue, so the user's latency is unaffected.
haiku-low.q9: The copy is dropped silently. The user is unaffected.
haiku-low.q10: Shadow results go to the prediction log. The daily job compares candidate items with what the active model returned for the same users. Where active predictions are stored is NOT STATED.
haiku-low.q11: Each version records its required features. Shadow workers and API instances run a feature check before starting or loading, and a switch is refused if the check fails.
haiku-low.q12: The active alias is moved back to previous, with no approval needed. Instances pick it up within one 15-second polling interval. If an instance cannot load previous, it keeps its current version and alerts.

sonnet.q1: The fallback popular-items list, marked as a fallback; the model is not called.
sonnet.q2: The store keeps serving what it has, but records older than 6 hours are treated as missing. Once a user's record is over 6 hours old, requests stop using it and return the marked fallback. The job failure raises an alert.
sonnet.q3: No, shadow output is never shown to a user. A shadow failure or slow run is logged as an error in the prediction log and never touches the user's response.
sonnet.q4: Users whose stable hash of user ID, modulo 100, is under 10 (about 10% of users). The same users are always in the group.
sonnet.q5: At least 7 days in shadow, error rate under 0.5%, p99 inference latency under 80 ms, and ML lead approval. The feature check for that version must also pass, or the switch is refused.
sonnet.q6: Undecided. Product has not decided whether an A/B test sits between shadow and the full switch. The plan does not choose. Until then promotion ends with an approved candidate and no switch.
sonnet.q7: Each instance polls the registry every 15 seconds. When the active alias points to a different version, it loads that version in the background, runs the feature check, and swaps only if the load and check succeed. No redeploy is needed.
sonnet.q8: The API puts the user ID and the features it already fetched on a shadow queue, so no new lookup is needed. It does this after responding and without waiting, and separate shadow workers run the candidate, so the user's latency is unaffected.
sonnet.q9: If the queue is full or unavailable, the copy is dropped silently. A failed or slow shadow run is recorded as an error in the log. The user is unaffected.
sonnet.q10: Only shadow results are in the prediction log (user ID, version, items, latency, error). Active predictions are not stated as recorded there. A daily job reads the log and reports days in shadow, error rate, p99 inference latency, and item overlap with what the active model returned for the same users. It writes the report where the ML lead can read it.
sonnet.q11: A feature check requires every required feature of the version, as recorded at registration, to exist in the online store. It runs on instances before swapping, so a failing instance keeps its current version and alerts. Shadow workers run it before starting, so the candidate does not run in shadow. The switch is also refused if the check fails.
sonnet.q12: The active alias is moved back to previous, with no approval needed. Instances poll every 15 seconds and so pick it up within one polling interval, inside the 1-minute limit, with no redeploy. If an instance cannot load previous, it keeps its current version and alerts.
